Ch8: 함정 구간 전수 보존 — 개구리 침실·침대·화덕·솥 침입, 모세의 시간 지정 제안, 개구리 더미·악취, 이는 마술사 실패('하나님의 하심'), 파리 재앙의 고센 제외·내일 표적, 사흘 길 예배 요구, 바로의 '너무 멀리 가지 말라'·'나를 위해 기도하라'
paragraphs: § Strike Two: Frogs

God said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him: God's Message — Release my people so they can worship me. If you refuse, I'm warning you: I'll hit the whole country with frogs. The Nile will swarm with frogs — they'll crawl into your houses, your bedrooms, your beds, your servants' rooms, all over the people, into your ovens and your pots and pans. They'll be all over you — frogs everywhere, on and in everything!"
God told Moses, "Tell Aaron: wave your staff over the rivers, canals, and ponds. Bring frogs up over Egypt."
Aaron stretched his staff over the waters of Egypt, and a huge mob of frogs came up and covered the whole country.
But the magicians did the same thing with their magic spells — they also brought frogs up over Egypt.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron in and said, "Pray to God to get rid of these frogs. I'll let the people go so they can sacrifice and worship God."
Moses said to Pharaoh, "Sure. You set the time — when do you want the frogs gone from you, your servants, your people, and your houses? You'll be rid of frogs, except the ones in the Nile."

"Make it tomorrow." Moses said, "Tomorrow it is — so you'll know there's no God like our God. The frogs will be gone — you, your houses, your servants, your people, all frog-free. The only frogs left will be in the Nile."

Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, and Moses prayed to God about the frogs he'd brought on Pharaoh. God answered Moses' prayer: the frogs died — houses, courtyards, fields, all frog-free. They piled the dead frogs in heaps, and the whole country stank of dead frogs.
But when Pharaoh saw he'd gotten some breathing room, he got stubborn again and wouldn't listen to Moses and Aaron. Just as God had said.
§ Strike Three: Gnats
God told Moses, "Tell Aaron: take your staff and strike the dust — the dust will turn into gnats all over Egypt."

He did it. Aaron grabbed his staff and struck the dust of the ground — it turned into gnats, gnats all over people and animals. All the dust of the ground turned into gnats, gnats everywhere in Egypt.
The magicians tried to make gnats with their spells, but this time they couldn't. Gnats were everywhere, all over people and animals.
The magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is God's doing." But Pharaoh was stubborn and wouldn't listen. Just as God had said.
§ Strike Four: Flies

God told Moses, "Get up early in the morning and confront Pharaoh as he goes down to the water. Tell him: God's Message — Release my people so they can worship me. If you don't release my people, I'll send swarms of flies on you, your servants, your people, and your houses. The Egyptians' houses — even the ground under their feet — will be thick with flies. But when it happens, I'll set Goshen apart as a safe zone, where my people live — no flies in Goshen. That'll prove I'm God, right here in this land. I'll make a sharp line between your people and mine. This sign happens tomorrow."
And God did exactly that. Thick swarms of flies filled Pharaoh's palace and his servants' houses. All over Egypt, the country was being wrecked by flies.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron in and said, "Fine, go. Sacrifice to your God — but do it here, in this country."

Moses said, "That wouldn't be smart. What we sacrifice to our God would deeply offend the Egyptians. If we openly sacrifice what offends them so much, they'll kill us. Let us go on a three-day journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to our God, just like he told us."
Pharaoh said, "OK. I'll let you go sacrifice to your God in the wilderness. Just don't go too far. And pray for me."
Moses said, "The moment I leave, I'll pray to God that tomorrow the flies leave you, your servants, and your people. But don't trick us and change your mind about letting us go sacrifice to God."

Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to God. God did what Moses asked — he got rid of the flies from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people. Not a single fly was left. But Pharaoh got stubborn again and wouldn't let the people go.
title: Strikes Two, Three, Four: Frogs, Gnats, Flies
